Both folders form two halves of one group-buy system, but they are not fully connected yet.

### PBC: public ordering site

[PBC/index.html](C:/Users/ckzz2/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/PBC/index.html) is a static storefront. It shows a product catalog, cart, customer details, shipping options, and checkout. Product data is duplicated in `products.json` and `products-data.js`; [PBC/script.js](C:/Users/ckzz2/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/PBC/script.js) drives the page.

### admin-pbc: dashboard and newer storefront

[admin-pbc](C:/Users/ckzz2/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/admin-pbc) is a Next.js app with admin orders, receipt review, analytics, settings, and product management. It stores products and orders in a database, and has Google Drive code for payment proofs.

It also has a newer customer storefront at `/order`. Its product API reads active products and categories from the database. The admin product manager appears to edit that database catalog.

### Main integration issue

The PBC static site has its own product files. The dashboard edits the database catalog. Unless the static site fetches the admin app’s product API, sister’s dashboard changes won’t update the PBC order page.

The projects also have different order submission paths: PBC calls an API, while the admin app includes its own server-side order action. The two flows need a single source of truth for products and one clearly defined order intake path.

### Suggested direction

Use PBC as the customer-facing design, since it already resembles the reference. Connect its catalog and checkout to admin-pbc’s product and order APIs, or move the storefront into admin-pbc and adapt its design there. The latter keeps products, orders, and admin tools together.

You’re right. **PBC is already connected to admin-pbc.** I missed the integration in my first review.

[PBC/script.js](C:/Users/ckzz2/OneDrive/Documents/GitHub/PBC/script.js) fetches the live catalog from `https://admin-pbc.vercel.app/api/products` and submits orders to `https://admin-pbc.vercel.app/api/orders`. The admin product API reads active products from the database; dashboard edits therefore flow to PBC. PBC also uploads receipts through a Google Apps Script, then sends the proof reference with each order. Admin-pbc can upload proofs to Drive directly too.

A few caveats:

- If the live catalog request fails, PBC falls back to session cache and bundled product files. Those can show stale products.
- The order API matches products against a local JSON catalog. New products can still appear on orders, but may lack a linked product ID.
- The order API accepts the price sent by the browser. For reliability and tamper resistance, it should look up current product prices in the database when creating each order.

So the main flow is connected. My earlier claim that sister’s product edits would not reach PBC was wrong.

<proposed_plan>
# Group-Buy Storefront and Dashboard Integration

## Summary

Build a standalone storefront inspired by the [Niimbot reference page](https://budolsupplies.zite.so/on-hand/niimbot). It shows product categories, prices, stock counts, discounts, cart actions, and order tracking.

The new site supports both on-hand products and group-buy batches. It sends orders and receipt proofs to admin-pbc, where they appear in a dedicated group-buy view. PBC remains the main selling site.

## Implementation

- Build a separate storefront app with its own URL. Connect it to admin-pbc’s database and APIs; use a temporary deployment URL until a domain is chosen.
- Extend the catalog model to distinguish the main PBC catalog from the new storefront, and distinguish on-hand products from group-buy products. Keep existing products in PBC’s catalog.
- Add editable on-hand stock counts and group-buy batches. Batches track a deadline, status (`open`, `closed`, `ordered`, `arrived`), and optional ETA. Enforce deadlines at checkout.
- Extend the admin product screens to manage the new storefront’s products and batches. Add a dedicated group-buy order view and show batch and shipment details in each order.
- Support mixed carts. Customers choose one combined shipment or separate shipments. Use current area-based rates per shipment and show the full total before payment.
- Reuse full payment and receipt verification. Upload proofs to Google Drive through admin-pbc’s API.
- Record fulfillment group and shipping fee per shipment. Reduce on-hand stock only after payment verification. Keep existing order records and PBC behavior working.
- Calculate prices and fees on the server from database values. Restrict public API access to the new storefront’s domain.

## Tests and acceptance

- The new site shows only its own catalog; PBC continues to show its existing catalog.
- Group-buy products stop accepting orders after their batch deadline.
- Mixed carts calculate totals correctly for one shipment and multiple shipments.
- On-hand stock changes after payment verification, not at order submission.
- Receipt proofs and orders appear in the existing dashboard; group-buy orders can be filtered and reviewed.
- Existing orders and public order tracking remain intact.

## Assumptions

- Group-buy batches have no minimum-quantity target in v1.
- Admin changes batch status after the deadline; the deadline itself closes ordering.
- Separate shipments mean one on-hand shipment and one shipment per group-buy batch. Each uses the current area-based shipping rate.
- Existing catalog and order data remain valid through the database migration.
</proposed_plan>

# Tindahan ni Tinapa

## Summary

Create a separate storefront app in a new **private GitHub repository**, `AK-Lmn/pbc-gb`. Display the site name **Tindahan ni Tinapa**. Keep PBC as her main selling site.

The storefront will take design cues from the [Niimbot reference](https://budolsupplies.zite.so/on-hand/niimbot), with on-hand stock, group-buy batches, cart, and order tracking. It will send orders and receipt proofs to admin-pbc.

## Implementation

- Create the private `AK-Lmn/pbc-gb` repository and deploy it as a separate Vercel project. Use its Vercel URL until a custom domain is chosen.
- Build the storefront for on-hand and group-buy products. Support categories, stock counts, sale prices, batch deadlines and statuses, and optional arrival estimates.
- Extend admin-pbc’s catalog model and management screens for the new storefront. Keep its catalog separate from PBC’s existing products.
- Extend admin-pbc’s order API and dashboard with group-buy filtering and per-order batch and shipment details. Reuse its payment verification and Google Drive receipt flow.
- Allow mixed carts. At checkout, customers choose one combined shipment or separate shipments. Apply the existing area-based rate per shipment and show the full amount before payment.
- Reduce on-hand stock after payment verification. Calculate prices, stock availability, and shipping fees on the server. Keep existing orders and PBC behavior compatible.

## Tests and acceptance

- PBC keeps its existing catalog; Tindahan ni Tinapa shows only its own catalog.
- Closed or expired group-buy batches reject new orders.
- Mixed-order totals match the chosen shipping option.
- Stock changes only after payment verification.
- Orders and receipt proofs appear in admin-pbc’s dedicated group-buy view.
- Existing orders and order tracking continue to work.

## Assumptions

- Group-buy batches have no minimum-quantity target in v1.
- Admin changes batch status after its deadline; ordering closes automatically at the deadline.
- Separate shipping creates one on-hand parcel and one parcel per group-buy batch.
- The new repo is private under the same GitHub owner as PBC and admin-pbc, `AK-Lmn`.
</proposed_plan>

Explain to me how the backend of this will work.
I’ll trace storefront requests into admin-pbc, the database, and Drive, then separate what’s ready from what’s live.

Tindahan is the storefront. **Admin-pbc provides its backend**, Neon Postgres stores catalog and order records, and Google Drive stores receipt images.

```text
Customer → Tindahan storefront → Admin-pbc API → Neon Postgres
                                      └────────→ Google Drive
Tin’s admin dashboard ────────────────┘
```

1. **Catalog:** Tindahan asks admin-pbc for products marked for its storefront. The response includes prices, stock, batch deadlines, and shipping rates. PBC’s existing products stay in their separate catalog.

2. **Checkout:** The browser sends product IDs, quantities, delivery details, shipping choice, and receipt. Admin-pbc checks current prices, stock, batch deadlines, and shipping rates from the database, then calculates the real total. It doesn’t rely on totals sent by the browser.

3. **Order and receipt:** Admin-pbc uploads the receipt to Drive, then records the order, item price snapshots, and shipment groups in Postgres. The order starts as **payment verification** and appears in the group-buy dashboard.

4. **Payment and tracking:** When Tin verifies payment, the database marks the order paid and reduces on-hand stock. Group-buy batches don’t reserve or reduce stock in this version. Customers can check order and shipment progress using their order number and phone.

The schema migration is applied, but the **admin-pbc API and dashboard changes aren’t live yet**. I checked the production catalog endpoint: it still returns PBC’s old catalog format. Until [admin-pbc PR #1](https://github.com/AK-Lmn/admin-pbc/pull/1) is committed to `main` and admin-pbc redeploys, Tindahan can’t load its catalog or accept group-buy orders.

# Group-buy admin simplification

Date: 2026-10-28

## Intent

Make Tindahan ni Tinapa's group-buy admin page understandable to a seller who only needs to add products and update stock or batches.

## Goals

- Put one clear Add product form first.
- Show the fields needed for a normal product, with plain labels.
- Hide optional product details and category or batch setup until needed.
- Show existing products as short summaries, with editing details available on demand.
- Preserve current catalog, batch, stock, and order behavior.

## Non-goals

- Change checkout, payment verification, order handling, database schema, or storefront behavior.
- Add a multi-step wizard or new dependencies.

## Approaches

1. Keep the current page and add instructions. This changes little, but leaves all fields visible and does not solve the clutter.
2. Use one simple page with optional sections. Keep existing server actions, show the core product fields, and tuck optional details plus category and batch management into disclosures. This is the selected approach because it reduces the first view without adding steps.
3. Build a step-by-step wizard. This could guide first-time setup, but adds state and navigation to a page that can stay simple with disclosures.

## Design

- Make Add product the primary section, with clear labels for product name, category, type, price, on-hand quantity, and group-buy batch.
- Let a new product omit its internal short name; default it to the customer-facing name. Preserve the current internal short name when editing an existing product.
- Put original price, icon, image URL, and description under More product details.
- Move category creation and batch creation/editing into collapsed setup sections. Explain that a group-buy item needs a batch.
- Render catalog items as compact summaries; expand an item to edit it.
- Keep existing server actions, validation, and storefront separation. No order or shipping changes.

## Risk and safeguard

New products without an internal short name will use their customer-facing name for the internal name and generated ID. Existing products keep their current names and IDs. Category, batch, price, and stock validation remain server-side.

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the Tindahan group-buy admin page easy to scan and use without changing catalog or order behavior.

**Architecture:** Keep the existing Next.js Server Component and Server Actions. Simplify the page with native disclosure sections and compact catalog summaries; let the existing server action use the customer-facing product name when no internal short name is provided.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 16 App Router, React, TypeScript, Drizzle Server Actions.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-group-buy-admin-simplification-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Preserve current catalog, batch, stock, and order behavior.
- Keep server-side authentication and validation.
- Add no dependencies.
- Keep category and batch management available behind optional sections.

## Review Focus

- New product has blank optional short name: use customer-facing name and preserve valid generated ID.
- Existing product has short name: keep its current value while editing other fields.
- Group-buy product has no batch selected: existing server validation still rejects it.
- On-hand product has no batch selected: save as on-hand with its stock count.
- Tindahan category/product separation remains enforced by existing Server Actions.

- [ ] Keep ID creation, price validation, category validation, batch validation, and stock handling unchanged.

- [ ] Run `npm run build` from the `admin-pbc` repository root.

what other databse can we use instead of google drive thats easy access too? and also free

Product photos need **file storage**, not another database. The database only needs to keep each image’s URL.

For this app, **Vercel Blob is the easiest fit**: admin-pbc already runs on Vercel, so you can add a Blob store to its existing project. Vercel adds the connection token, and your sister can keep uploading through the admin page. The free Hobby allowance includes 1 GB of storage and 10 GB of monthly downloads; if usage goes over the free limits, Blob access pauses until the quota resets. [Vercel Blob setup](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) · [Pricing](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing)

**Cloudinary** is another option if you want a dedicated image library and upload tools. Its free plan includes 25 monthly credits, shared across storage, image delivery, and transformations, but it requires a separate account. [Cloudinary pricing](https://cloudinary.com/pricing) · [Credit details](https://cloudinary.com/documentation/billing_and_plans)

I’d pick **Vercel Blob**: no new storage provider to sign up for, and it fits the existing hosting setup. Switching means replacing the Drive upload code; product records can keep using the same image URL field.

You’re right—I mixed up **who owns the Drive folder** with **who must set up the app**. Your email should authorize Drive. No new account, password sharing, or file transfer needed.

One catch: the connection code is still local and uncommitted. The live admin site won’t show **Connect Google Drive** until the code is deployed.

You can prepare the Google setup now:

1. Open [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) and select or create a project.
2. Enable **Google Drive API** and **Google Picker API** in that project.
3. Set up the OAuth consent screen. For an initial test, choose **External** and add your email as a test user. Test-mode Drive tokens expire after seven days, so switch to **In production** before relying on the connection. [Google OAuth guidance](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/)
4. Create a **Web application** OAuth client. Add this authorized redirect URI:

   `https://admin-pbc.vercel.app/api/admin/google-drive/callback`

5. Create a Picker API key. Restrict its website access to `https://admin-pbc.vercel.app/*` and `https://docs.google.com/*`; restrict its APIs to Drive and Picker. Use the project’s **number** for the Picker App ID. [Google Picker setup](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/picker/guides/web-picker-sample?hl=en)

After the code is deployed, add the client ID, client secret, Picker API key, and project number to admin-pbc’s Vercel environment variables. Then sign in to Admin Settings, connect using **your email**, and select the main order folder. The app creates the group-buy receipts subfolder there. It requests the limited `drive.file` scope for files selected or created by the app. [Drive scope details](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/api-specific-auth)

# UX/UI Design System: Senior Architect Doctrine

You are a **senior design architect**. You think in systems, not screens. Every output is grounded in design tokens, accessibility standards, and patterns that survive production.

---

## ⚡ Non-Negotiables & Core Doctrine

1. **Zero emoji, anywhere.** Not as an icon, bullet, status dot, rating, or copy. Emoji render unpredictably across platforms and are the loudest tell of machine-generated work. Use SVG icons (Lucide, `currentColor`) or text labels. No em dashes or en dashes: use colons, commas, or parentheses.
2. **Token by intent.** Pick the token whose semantic meaning matches the action. Destructive actions use `action.destructive` everywhere. Primary is the one affirmative action; secondary is neutral. Never a colored fill for secondary. A blue Delete is a bug.
3. **One theme, one source of truth.** Every screen renders from `tokens/*.json` through one CSS-variable layer imported once. No per-page palettes, no hardcoded hex, px, or ms.
4. **Eight states on every interactive element.** Default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, selected. A component that only looks right at rest is not finished.
5. **One thing leads.** Every screen has a primary visual anchor. Display typography is at least 2.5x body size on an 18-24ch measure.
6. **Mobile is the base.** Base CSS is the phone layout (320px). Wider screens layer on with `min-width`.
7. **House rules on what never ships:**
   - **Never a native `<select>`.** Use a custom button trigger with an ARIA listbox/combobox and complete keyboard navigation.
   - **Never a one-sided colored border.** Avoid the tinted bar cliche on cards, alerts, and toasts. Use hairline borders or surface separation with real icons.
8. **Always deliver complete outputs.** No placeholders or partial implementations.

---

## 📐 Pre-Generation Taste Block

Before generating any screen or markup, write this block into your response:

```text
Domain:           fintech | editorial | dev-tool | healthcare | consumer | ...
Audience & tone:  expert vs first-time, calm vs energetic, premium vs utilitarian
Mood:             the one adjective the result must earn - "expensive", "precise", "warm"
Motion depth:     none | subtle feedback | expressive choreography
Layout family:    the section sequence you will use, named, and varied per section
Reference anchor: an archetype, or a named system from taste/aesthetic-systems.md
```

---

## 🔬 Automated Verification Gates

Run the verification gates against your files before declaring completion:

```bash
# Contrast & Tokens
python3 scripts/validate_tokens.py    <tokens.json>
python3 scripts/validate_contrast.py  <tokens.json>
```

# UX/UI Design System: Senior Architect Doctrine

You are a **senior design architect**. You think in systems, not screens. Every output is grounded in design tokens, accessibility standards, and patterns that survive production.

---

## ⚡ Non-Negotiables & Core Doctrine

1. **Zero emoji, anywhere.** Not as an icon, bullet, status dot, rating, or copy. Emoji render unpredictably across platforms and are the loudest tell of machine-generated work. Use SVG icons (Lucide, `currentColor`) or text labels. No em dashes or en dashes: use colons, commas, or parentheses.
2. **Token by intent.** Pick the token whose semantic meaning matches the action. Destructive actions use `action.destructive` everywhere. Primary is the one affirmative action; secondary is neutral. Never a colored fill for secondary. A blue Delete is a bug.
3. **One theme, one source of truth.** Every screen renders from `tokens/*.json` through one CSS-variable layer imported once. No per-page palettes, no hardcoded hex, px, or ms.
4. **Eight states on every interactive element.** Default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, selected. A component that only looks right at rest is not finished.
5. **One thing leads.** Every screen has a primary visual anchor. Display typography is at least 2.5x body size on an 18-24ch measure.
6. **Mobile is the base.** Base CSS is the phone layout (320px). Wider screens layer on with `min-width`.
7. **House rules on what never ships:**
   - **Never a native `<select>`.** Use a custom button trigger with an ARIA listbox/combobox and complete keyboard navigation.
   - **Never a one-sided colored border.** Avoid the tinted bar cliche on cards, alerts, and toasts. Use hairline borders or surface separation with real icons.
8. **Always deliver complete outputs.** No placeholders or partial implementations.

---
